note: Triennial election of the county council, 1936: nominations received 28 April 1936; no poll in the county. In Richhill, vacant by the death of T. H. Hardy, D.L., both nominees (Thomas James Spence and W. J. Black, J.P., both Unionists) withdrew, leaving the seat to be filled by co-option (Armagh Guardian, 8 May 1936, p. 3). Returned unopposed. Only Locke was nominated; the second retiring member, A. L. Martin, was deemed to be re-elected (no label printed for him).
